$comment: Plain-English translations (spec §3.2). Keys are lowercase; clause bodies reference them with [[term]] or [[display text|key]].

terms.indemnification: If someone sues you because of something the other party did, they cover your legal bills and any damages.
terms.operating agreement: The internal rulebook for an LLC: who owns what, who decides what, and what happens if someone leaves.
terms.registered agent: A person or company with a physical address in the state who officially receives legal mail for you.
terms.governing law: Which state's law a judge uses to interpret this contract if there is a dispute.
terms.severability: If a court strikes one clause, the rest of the contract still stands.
terms.vesting: You earn your ownership over time instead of getting it all on day one.
terms.cliff: A waiting period at the start of vesting. Leave before the cliff and you keep nothing.
terms.buy-sell: The rules for what happens to someone's ownership stake if they quit, die, divorce, or go bankrupt.
terms.charging order: A creditor chasing an owner's personal debt can only intercept that owner's distributions — they cannot seize the business itself.
terms.foreign qualification: Registering to do business in a state other than the one you formed in. "Foreign" means out-of-state, not out-of-country.
terms.fiduciary duty: A legal obligation to act in the company's interest rather than your own.
terms.pro rata: Split in proportion to ownership — own 30%, get 30%.
terms.quorum: The minimum number of people who must show up before a vote counts.
terms.dissolution: Formally shutting the company down and dividing up what is left.
terms.capital contribution: The money or property an owner puts into the business in exchange for their stake.
terms.right of first refusal: Before selling your stake to an outsider, you must offer it to the other owners on the same terms first.
terms.drag-along: If the majority votes to sell the company, minority owners are required to sell too.
terms.tag-along: If the majority sells, minority owners get to join the sale on the same terms.
terms.work made for hire: Work that belongs to the company from the moment it is created, rather than to the person who made it.
terms.business associate agreement: A HIPAA-required contract with any vendor that will touch patient health information.
terms.section 83(b) election: A form you file with the IRS within 30 days to pay tax on your shares now, while they are cheap, instead of later when they may be worth much more.
terms.par value: A nominal per-share price with no relationship to what the shares are worth. It exists for accounting and franchise tax math.
terms.preferred stock: A class of shares with rights ordinary shares do not have — typically getting paid back first in a sale.
terms.authorized shares: The ceiling on how many shares the company may issue. Issuing more requires amending the charter.
terms.good standing: Confirmation from the state that your filings and fees are current. Financings and bank accounts depend on it.
terms.piercing the veil: A court setting aside your limited liability because the company was not run as a separate business from its owners.
terms.at-will employment: Either side can end the employment relationship at any time, for any lawful reason or no reason.
terms.exempt employee: An employee who is not entitled to overtime because of their duties and salary. Job title alone does not decide this.
terms.retainage: Money a customer holds back from each payment until the job is finished and accepted.
terms.mechanics lien: A claim a contractor can record against the property itself when they have not been paid.
terms.conflict of laws: The rules a court uses to decide which state's law governs when more than one could apply.
terms.confidential information: Information one side shares that the other must keep to themselves. What counts is defined in the contract, not by intuition.
terms.residuals: A clause letting the receiving side keep using what their people remember, without notes. Generous to the receiver and easy to abuse.
terms.consequential damages: Knock-on losses — lost profits, lost business — as opposed to the direct cost of the problem itself. Usually excluded.
terms.limitation of liability: A ceiling on how much one side can owe the other, no matter how bad the outcome.
terms.indemnify: To cover someone else's losses and legal costs when a third party comes after them.
terms.service level agreement: A promise about how well the service will perform — uptime, response time — with a stated consequence if it does not.
terms.force majeure: Events outside anyone's control that excuse performance. It suspends obligations; it does not cancel them.
terms.subprocessor: A vendor your vendor uses to handle data on your behalf. You inherit the risk without picking them.
terms.data controller: The party that decides why and how personal data is processed.
terms.data processor: The party that processes personal data on the controller's instructions, without deciding the purpose.
terms.standard contractual clauses: Pre-approved contract language that makes it lawful to move personal data out of certain jurisdictions.
terms.change order: A signed amendment to the scope, schedule, or price. Without one, extra work is usually free work.
terms.acceptance criteria: The objective test a deliverable has to pass before it counts as delivered and payable.
terms.deliverable: A specific, identified thing being handed over — as opposed to general effort.
terms.statement of work: The short document holding scope, schedule, and price, sitting under a master agreement that holds the legal terms.
terms.order of precedence: Which document wins when two of them say different things.
terms.background ip: Intellectual property a party already owned before the engagement. It stays theirs.
terms.injunctive relief: A court order to stop doing something, rather than money after the fact.
terms.warranty disclaimer: A statement that no promises are being made beyond the ones written down.
terms.security incident: Unauthorized access to or disclosure of data. The contract usually defines it more precisely than intuition would.
terms.personal data: Information relating to an identifiable person. Broader than most people expect — device identifiers usually count.
terms.termination for convenience: The right to end the contract without anyone having done anything wrong.
terms.survival: The provisions that keep operating after the contract ends, such as confidentiality and limitation of liability.
terms.non-solicitation: A promise not to hire the other side's people, or not to approach their customers.
terms.most favored nation: A promise that no other customer gets a better price.
terms.cyber liability insurance: Coverage for the costs of a data breach — notification, forensics, and claims.
terms.source code escrow: Source code held by a third party and released to the customer if the vendor fails or stops supporting it.
terms.net 30: Payment is due 30 days after the invoice date.
terms.uptime: The percentage of time a service is available, measured over a stated period.
terms.assignment: Handing your side of a contract to someone else. Usually needs the other party's consent, with a carve-out for being acquired.
terms.abc test: California's three-part test for contractor status. All three parts must be met, and part B — the work sits outside the hiring company's own line of business — defeats most engagements.
terms.exempt salary threshold: The minimum salary an employee must earn before they can be exempt from overtime. In California it is a multiple of the state minimum wage, so it rises every January.
terms.reporting time pay: Pay owed when an employee shows up for a scheduled shift and is sent home early or given no work.
terms.split shift: A workday broken by an unpaid, non-meal gap. California owes a premium when it happens.
terms.iipp: Injury and Illness Prevention Program — the written safety program Cal/OSHA requires of every California employer, regardless of size or industry.
terms.workplace violence prevention plan: A written plan, training, and incident log California requires of most employers, separate from the general safety program.
terms.cfra: California Family Rights Act — job-protected family and medical leave, which attaches at five employees rather than the federal fifty.
terms.pregnancy disability leave: Up to four months of job-protected leave for pregnancy-related disability in California. Separate from, and stackable with, family leave.
terms.cal-cobra: California's continuation coverage law for employers too small for federal COBRA.
terms.calsavers: California's state-run retirement savings program. Employers without their own plan must register rather than opt out.
terms.pay data report: An annual filing of pay bands by race, ethnicity, and sex for each job category, required of larger California employers.
terms.wage theft notice: A written notice California requires at hire, stating pay rate, pay day, employer identity, and workers' compensation carrier.
terms.fair chance act: California's ban-the-box law. Conviction history cannot be asked about or considered until after a conditional offer, and rejecting on that basis requires a written individualized assessment.
terms.section 1542: The California Civil Code provision a release must expressly waive, or the release does not cover claims the signer did not know about.
terms.automatic renewal law: California's statute governing subscriptions that renew on their own — it requires clear disclosure, affirmative consent, and cancellation that is as easy as signup.
terms.section 2115: The California rule applying core California corporate law to an out-of-state corporation whose business and shareholders are predominantly Californian.
terms.franchise tax: California's annual tax on the privilege of doing business in the state. It is owed whether or not the business made money.
terms.fictitious business name: A trade name different from the entity's legal name. California requires a county filing and newspaper publication.
terms.seller's permit: California's registration to sell tangible goods, required before the first sale, not after.
terms.labor code 925: The California rule that an employer generally cannot require a California employee to litigate outside California or under another state's law.
terms.individualized assessment: The written, case-specific analysis California requires before rejecting an applicant over a conviction.
terms.paga: California's Private Attorneys General Act. It lets an employee sue on the state's behalf for labor code violations across the whole workforce, which turns a small individual claim into a company-wide one.
terms.cal-warn: California's plant closing and mass layoff notice law. It reaches further than the federal version — relocations and terminations count, and part-time employees count toward the threshold.
terms.pay equity: California's requirement of equal pay for substantially similar work, where differences must be justified by specific listed factors and prior salary is not one of them.
terms.cipa: California's wiretapping statute. Written for phone taps, it is now the basis for a large volume of claims about website session recording and third-party trackers.
terms.unruh act: California's civil rights statute. It carries statutory damages per violation and is the usual vehicle for website accessibility claims in the state.
terms.casp: A Certified Access Specialist. California commercial leases must state whether the property has been inspected by one, and the answer changes who carries accessibility risk.
terms.song-beverly: California's consumer warranty statute. It gives buyers of consumer goods rights beyond the written warranty, including a refund-or-replace remedy.
terms.dark pattern: An interface designed so the user's choice is not really free. Under California privacy law, consent obtained that way is not consent.
terms.day of rest: California's rule that employees are entitled to one day off in seven, with a narrow exemption for short workweeks.
terms.reporting: Notifying a government agency of something the law requires you to report, on that agency's timetable rather than your own.
